rv.q: It's a gripping, socio-political railroad powered by Pike's breathless performance.
It's a roller coaster of a show for which Pike may well win an Olivier Award this coming Sunday.
Take this as a story about the wild challenge of balancing morality and legality, of protecting your children and letting them go, and you have something fine indeed.
The two men provide sterling support but it’s Pike’s night - a triumphant, freewheeling turn from an actress at the height of her powers.
It's familiar material, but Pike's humour and commitment and the confidence of the production elevate it.
It is slick (perhaps too much so) and entertaining, but also has the courage of its convictions in the questions it raises.
Inter Alia shows every mother’s worst nightmare — and proves that even when you do everything ‘right’, your child is still capable of committing terrible wrongs.
Even if it’s sometimes awkward and overwrought, it’ll be interesting to see what comes next.
At its heart is a compelling character study of a woman forced to be everything at once, anchored by Pike, a clear favourite to win the Best Actress Olivier this Sunday.
Pike never misses a beat in this fast-paced show and is absolutely captivating to watch.
So shattering, it renews my faith in theatre while simultaneously destroying my faith in parenthood and humanity.
Pike is an absolute force. Authentic in her role, she is entirely convincing as Judge and mother.
Believe the hype. Inter Alia will have you feeling every emotion possible and you'll think about it for days.
It's sexy, provocative, and totally unnerving.
Pike powers through the evening in what is surely one of the best performances of the year.
Despite a few imperfections, Inter Alia is an exhilarating and relevant examination of law and morality, feminism and motherhood, and gender politics within the home and the courts of the land.
